title: Password Authentication Service Boundary
objective: Compose the canonical PrincipalRepository, PasswordCredentialRepository, and PasswordHasher into a provider-neutral password authentication service that resolves successful credentials to PrincipalId while preserving generic failure behavior, disabled-principal rejection, timing-oriented dummy verification for unknown identities, and strict separation from HTTP, sessions, and Sesh product authorization.
authenticationFlow: Normalize the supplied email using the canonical credential normalizer.
Verify supplied password against stored password hash.
Resolve AuthenticatedPrincipal by the credential PrincipalId.
Require the principal to be active.
Return canonical PrincipalId only after successful credential and principal verification.

enumerationResistance.unknownEmail: Runs PasswordHasher verification against an injected valid dummy password hash before returning generic invalid-credentials.
enumerationResistance.malformedEmail: Runs PasswordHasher verification against the dummy password hash before returning generic invalid-credentials.
enumerationResistance.wrongPassword: Returns the same generic invalid-credentials code/message.
enumerationResistance.disabledPrincipal: Returns the same generic invalid-credentials code/message and does not expose account status.

operationalFailures.credentialRepository: Maps non-not-found repository failures to unavailable.
operationalFailures.principalRepository: Maps missing or failed principal resolution after a verified credential to unavailable because this represents persistence inconsistency or infrastructure failure.
operationalFailures.passwordHasher: Maps operational hashing exceptions to unavailable.
operationalFailures.clientDisclosure: Internal repository/provider error details are not surfaced by the authentication service.

rehash.rule: SESH-020 does not silently rewrite credential hashes during authentication.

principal.identity: PrincipalId remains the only canonical identity returned by authentication.

currentRiverOsAuth.rule: Existing River OS shared-key/boolean authentication remains an operator gate and MUST NOT be treated as canonical PrincipalId authentication.

sessionBoundary.requirement: The next session architecture must carry or resolve canonical PrincipalId rather than a boolean authenticated flag.

seshAuthorizationBoundary.rule: Successful password authentication does not itself establish SeshCreatorId, project ownership, collaborator access, publishing rights, management rights, or other Sesh authority.

nextSlice.title: Authenticated Principal Session Architecture
scope: Define the canonical authenticated session model.
Define how a session carries or resolves PrincipalId.
Keep session identity distinct from PrincipalId.
Define session creation, lookup, expiry, invalidation, and disabled-principal behavior.
Define session fixation and rotation requirements.
Reuse shared River session infrastructure where appropriate without reusing the River OS boolean session as product identity.
Do not create public login or registration endpoints yet.
Do not create PrincipalId to SeshCreatorId mapping.
Do not expose creator-owned Sesh APIs.
Do not mutate production identity data.
